one_line: Agent-assisted audio editing that finds and iterates short story cuts from long recordings.
what_it_does: Searches transcripts and audio energy, proposes non-contiguous clips, trims and plays cuts, and incorporates human steering.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent structured access to transcript, audio-derived moments, clip assembly, playback, and human feedback; generic UI driving would be markedly less precise.

findEnergyMoments uses RMS envelope rather than transcript text
proposals remain pending for human review
execution_rationale: The concept and interface are coherent and intentional, but the submitted frame sheets mainly show branding, timeline concepts, and tool registration rather than a complete audible end-to-end edit.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows 38-minute/547-line source and selected timeline markers
Frame sheet shows Cutroom UI and document.modelContext registration
impact_rationale: Editors and podcasters have a concrete high-friction problem: finding compelling moments in long recordings while preserving taste and review.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies long-form podcast editing and difficulty judging clips without hearing them
Audio-energy and steerable pending clips directly address discovery and iteration
creativity_rationale: Treating the agent as a taste-search partner that can hear delivery, rather than an automatic script writer, is a fresh and well-developed interaction model.

one_line: Pre-context prompt-injection scanner for text, files, URLs, and MCP server metadata.
what_it_does: Provides read-only WebMCP scanning tools and compact verdicts before untrusted content reaches agent context.
leverage_rationale: The pre-context boundary and opaque file workflow address a security limitation that ordinary UI-driving agents cannot reliably solve after reading hostile content.
leverage_evidence: Four typed tools scan text, MCP servers, URLs, and files
Claims candidate contents stay out of model context until verdict
Frame montage shows warning and success/failure states
execution_rationale: The product scope, interface, repository, and security story align, though no video was submitted and frame details are small.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot identifies PatrAgent and Scan before context
Frame montage shows repeated scan UI with red and green outcomes
Public repository and live demo are reported
impact_rationale: Agent users and developers face a specific consequential problem—prompt injection in external content—and the proposed pre-context screening directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Supports text, files, URLs, and MCP metadata
Explicitly targets hostile content before context ingestion
creativity_rationale: A security gate for WebMCP content is a timely, useful synthesis with a clear boundary-oriented interaction, though the scanner category is recognizable.
creativity_evidence: Same security layer is exposed to people and agents
Opaque identifiers and compact verdicts are a thoughtful interaction detail
usability_note: Multiple scan modalities and clear result states suggest usable flow; small evidence limits assessment.
red_flags: No submitted video; security efficacy and false-positive behavior are not demonstrated
standouts: Public repo plus live demo claim
advance_reason: High-impact and high-leverage security application with coherent evidence.

what_it_does: Presents an avatar-based agent that listens, responds, reacts, and performs agentic tasks through browser tools.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP can make tool calling reliable, but the primary novelty is the embodied interface; a general agent could achieve many task outcomes with friction.
leverage_evidence: Claims 10+ WebMCP tools
Frame sheet shows avatar, dialogue panel, controls, and changing environments
execution_rationale: The visual product identity is coherent, but static frames do not establish voice, gaze, gesture animation, or a completed tool task.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets consistently show Persona avatar/chat UI
Devpost packaging lists embodied capabilities
impact_rationale: There is real value for users seeking accessible, expressive interaction, but the concrete audience problem and task benefits are less specific than the presentation.
impact_evidence: Pitch addresses disconnection of text-box interaction
Interface visibly combines avatar and dialogue
creativity_rationale: Embodied persona, scene changes, and multimodal social signaling are a memorable interaction model for browser agents.
creativity_evidence: Frame labels emphasize SPEAK, LISTEN, and REACT
Avatar and environment are integrated into the agent UI

one_line: Natural-language QR and barcode generation with WebMCP-accessible customization and export.

Natural-language request maps to structured QR payload

execution_evidence: Facts report demo_alive=dead
No video frame sheets submitted

impact_rationale: Small businesses and everyday users have a clear need for easy QR/barcode creation, though the category is well served.
impact_evidence: Supports Wi-Fi and customizable vector outputs

one_line: Traceable public-comment research workspace for agent-assisted evidence gathering and cited briefs.
what_it_does: Searches Regulations.gov comments, pins exact excerpts to a shared evidence board, supports human verification, and prepares cited briefs.
leverage_rationale: The central value is shared live state: the agent searches and pins evidence while the analyst verifies/removes it and the agent reads those decisions. This is difficult to replicate comparably through generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: WebMCP connects agent to analyst’s live evidence board
Pinned excerpts remain source-traceable and reviewable
Unreviewed evidence is kept out of exports
execution_rationale: The description is coherent and technically specific, but there are no gallery images or video frames, so end-to-end execution is only claimed.
execution_evidence: Live demo reported alive
Packet describes pagination, quote validation, review gating, and cited export
impact_rationale: Policy researchers and analysts have a concrete high-volume evidence-traceability problem, and the workflow directly preserves source links and human review.
impact_evidence: Targets thousands of public comments
Exact excerpts and cited brief are core outputs
creativity_rationale: The shared evidence board and explicit review boundary are a strong, original collaboration model for agents in public-comment research.
creativity_evidence: Agent and analyst jointly curate evidence before brief generation
Traceability is built into the interaction rather than appended
usability_note: The described board/review flow is promising; no visual evidence to assess polish.
red_flags: No gallery images or submitted video; core claims are not visually demonstrated
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and credible research impact outweigh thin execution evidence.

one_line: Agent-adapted interfaces that simplify complex forms around a person’s situation and intent.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes the service’s rules and structure for reliable contextual adaptation, changing the interface itself rather than merely filling fields.

execution_evidence: Gallery includes initial, simplified, and final versions
Frame sheets show dark chat UI and responses
impact_rationale: People with ADHD or anyone facing confusing public-service forms have a concrete accessibility and comprehension problem addressed by contextual simplification.
impact_evidence: Fictitious repair-support form demonstrates complexity reduction
Pitch explicitly centers personal needs and intent
creativity_rationale: Adapting the service interface itself around user context is a fresh alternative to the usual agent-autofill pattern.
creativity_evidence: Purpose is not to remove the user from the decision loop
usability_note: Before/after simplification is legible and user-centered; real-world generalization is unverified.

one_line: Interactive playground showing how malicious content attacks WebMCP agents and how defenses change outcomes.
what_it_does: Lets developers attack, toggle defenses, rerun scenarios, and compare prompt-injection results in a controlled support-ticket setting.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP makes the security failure concrete in the agent-tool boundary and enables repeatable toggled experiments, though a similar playground could use other agent APIs.
leverage_evidence: Pitch centers malicious support ticket weaponizing WebMCP
Frame sheets show a dark tool/security demonstration interface
Attack/toggle/rerun/compare is a structured loop
execution_rationale: The educational scenario, controls, and defensive comparison appear coherent and the live demo is reported alive; stills do not prove actual agent execution.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show multiple playground states
Public repo and live demo reported
Scope is focused on one demonstrable threat
impact_rationale: Developers building agentic web apps have a real need to understand and test prompt-injection defenses, and an executable demonstration can teach better than documentation.
impact_evidence: Targets WebMCP security guidance gap
Compares attack success with defenses
creativity_rationale: Turning an often abstract security warning into an interactive adversarial playground is memorable and appropriately ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Red-team framing explores the non-happy-path side of WebMCP
usability_note: Focused experimental controls should be understandable; exact results are not readable in all frames.
red_flags: Static evidence does not establish actual model behavior or defense coverage
advance_reason: Strong educational impact and creative security demonstration with credible product evidence.

what_it_does: Keeps the article navigable, hides sentences judged to spoil the reader, records reasons, and lets the reader override masks.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP enables the agent to write personalized spoiler rules into the live page while the page supplies article structure and persists the policy across linked articles; the shared division of knowledge is central.
leverage_evidence: Transcript shows 49 sentences opened in one call based on watched seasons
Rules and reasons remain in the page and apply to later articles
Reader can override hidden content while seeing counts and reasons

execution_evidence: Video exists with 155 seconds
Transcript documents end-to-end Breaking Bad example
Frame sheets submitted and live demo reported alive
impact_rationale: Viewers researching shows, films, books, or games have a clear desire to learn facts without accidental endings; the solution preserves the source article rather than replacing it with a summary.
impact_evidence: Specific Wikipedia spoiler problem
Sentence-level reversible masking and season-aware personalization
creativity_rationale: The page/agent division of labor and persistent, explainable, reversible spoiler policy is genuinely novel, memorable, and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: Agent knows reader history while page knows article semantics

usability_note: Visible counts, reasons, and tap-to-reveal preserve control and make the masking model legible.
standouts: Reversible, explainable privacy-like control over content

impact_evidence: Benefits-style claim models realistic Universal Credit wording

Uses existing logged-in session without API keys
